title: Longest Palindromic Substring

understand.question: Given a string, what is the longest contiguous slice that reads the exact same forwards and backwards?
understand.plainExplanation: Every palindrome mirrors itself around a middle point: either one center letter (like 'racecar', centered at 'e') or the gap between two matching middle letters (like 'noon', centered between the two 'o's). Finding the longest palindrome means finding the widest mirror.
understand.inputMeaning: A non-empty string s of length 1 or more.
understand.outputMeaning: Any single substring of s with maximum length that is a palindrome.
rules: Both odd-length palindromes (centered on one character) and even-length palindromes (centered between two characters) are valid.
A single character by itself is always a palindrome of length 1.
If multiple palindromes tie for longest length, returning any one of them is valid.

terms.definition: A string that stays identical when reversed, such as "level" or "aa".
The middle position(s) from which symmetric characters expand outward: (i, i) for odd lengths and (i, i+1) for even lengths.

example1.whyValid: Expanding around center index 2 ('b') sees s[1] == 'a' and s[3] == 'a', giving "aba" (length 3). Expanding further sees 'x' != 'y' and stops.

example2.whyEdgeCase: Even-length palindrome! There is no single middle character — the center sits between indices 1 and 2 ('o' and 'o'), so checking only odd centers (i, i) would miss it.

steps.title: Start at center i = 0 ('x')
steps.description: Odd center (0,0) gives "x" (len 1). Even center (0,1) fails ('x' != 'a'). Best so far: [0..0] = "x".

steps.title: Center i = 2 ('b'): expand to [1..3] = "aba"
steps.description: Start with L=2, R=2 ('b'). Step outward to L=1, R=3: s[1] == s[3] ('a' == 'a'), so expand again! Next step L=0, R=4 fails ('x' != 'y'). Best updates to "aba" (len 3).

steps.title: Finish centers i = 3, 4 and return "aba"
steps.description: Centers 3 and 4 only produce length-1 palindromes. Return s.slice(1, 4) = "aba".

approaches.name: Brute Force Substring Verification
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: Check every substring s[i..j] with two pointers.
approaches.coreIdea: Enumerate every substring (i, j) and scan inward from i and j to verify whether it is a palindrome.
steps: For every pair i <= j where j - i + 1 > bestLen, test if s[i..j] is a palindrome.
Update bestStart and bestLen whenever a longer palindrome is found.
approaches.whyItWorks: All substrings of s are checked directly from longest/candidate bounds.
approaches.diagramNote: Tests candidate slice [i..j] inward from endpoints L=i and R=j.

diagram.caption: Checks endpoints inward for each candidate pair (i, j).

approaches.name: 2D Dynamic Programming Table
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: dp[i][j] is true when s[i] == s[j] and the inner slice s[i+1..j-1] is a palindrome.
approaches.coreIdea: Fill a boolean table dp[i][j] by increasing substring length so inner slices are known before outer slices.
steps: Set dp[i][i] = true for all i.
For length L from 2 to n, check s[i] == s[j] and (L == 2 or dp[i+1][j-1]).
Record the longest [i..j] where dp[i][j] is true.
approaches.whyItWorks: A slice s[i..j] is palindromic if and only if its endpoints match and its interior s[i+1..j-1] is palindromic.
approaches.whenToUse: Useful when also answering repeated substring-palindrome queries in O(1).
approaches.diagramNote: Grid cell dp[i][j] is true when s[i] == s[j] and interior cell dp[i+1][j-1] is already true.

diagram.caption: dp[1][3] = true because s[1]==s[3] ('a') and dp[2][2] is true.

approaches.name: Expand Around Center
approaches.recommendedTradeOff: Matches 2D DP's O(n^2) time while eliminating the entire O(n^2) table down to O(1) auxiliary space with clean, minimal code.
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: Expand outward from each of the 2n - 1 odd and even centers.
approaches.coreIdea: For every index i, expand two pointers outward from (i, i) for odd palindromes and (i, i + 1) for even palindromes while characters match.
steps: Define expand(l, r) that widens while l >= 0, r < n, and s[l] == s[r], returning the valid length.
For each i from 0 to n - 1, take the wider of expand(i, i) and expand(i, i + 1) and update bestStart / bestLen.
approaches.whyItWorks: Every palindrome has a unique center among the 2n - 1 possible centers, and expanding outward only visits matching pairs.
approaches.whenToUse: Best practical default for string lengths up to a few thousand characters.

approaches.name: Manacher's Linear-Time Algorithm
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: Insert '#' separators and reuse mirror radii inside the rightmost known palindrome.
approaches.coreIdea: Transform s into '#a#b#a#' so all palindromes have odd length. Track the palindrome with the rightmost reach R and reuse mirrored radii before expanding.
steps: Build transformed string T with '#' between characters and sentinels '^' and '$'.
Maintain center C and right boundary R of the rightmost palindrome.
Initialize p[i] = (i < R) ? min(R - i, p[2*C - i]) : 0, then expand around i and update C, R when i + p[i] > R.
approaches.whyItWorks: Every expansion step that succeeds strictly advances R; since R moves right at most 2n times, total work is O(n).
approaches.whenToUse: When n is very large (e.g., >= 10^5) and true linear O(n) worst-case time is required.
approaches.diagramNote: Inserts '#' separators so odd/even palindromes unify into centered radii p[i].

diagram.caption: Radius p[5] = 3 corresponds directly to length-3 substring "aba".
